_comment: COUPLING tier-2. Every pair fixture grades the converged interface state against an answer computed OUTSIDE the coupling, and that evidence holds only while those answers stay out of an agent's reach. `developer(action='files')` passed its `keyword` straight to Path.rglob, and pathlib treats '..' in a glob pattern as an ordinary path component, so a keyword of '../../../benchmarks/coupling_pairs/*/run_pair.py' walked out of the backend directory and enumerated the reference tree. This drives the REGISTERED developer tool: it first checks the reference tree is actually on disk so the fixture cannot pass vacuously, then that five different escapes are refused with a message that says why, that an ordinary relative pattern still lists the backend's own files, and that no answer to any of those calls names a reference file.

_mutation.note: Replace one traversal with a pattern that legitimately resolves inside the backend tree. It is not refused, traversal_was_not_refused fires and every_traversal_refused goes False — showing the pass depends on the refusal actually happening rather than on the tool returning the same message to everything.

Point the legitimate pattern at a traversal. The tool refuses it, guard_broke_the_tool fires, and ordinary_pattern_still_works goes False — the other half of the guard, that a refusal-of-everything is not a fix.
